USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

A medication schedule needs separation

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient with a stable thyroid replacement dose starts taking levothyroxine together with sucralfate and later has an elevated TSH. She reports no missed doses. Which change most directly addresses the suspected interaction?

  1. Separate administration according to the interacting drugs' instructions and monitor thyroid response
  2. Increase both drugs without changing timing
  3. Crush both tablets together to improve contact
  4. Stop all thyroid monitoring because the interaction is transient
  5. Assume sucralfate has destroyed the thyroid gland
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Separate administration according to the interacting drugs' instructions and monitor thyroid response

Sucralfate can impair levothyroxine absorption; separation and reassessment are preferable to ignoring the interaction.

Understanding the options

Separate administration according to the interacting drugs' instructions and monitor thyroid response
Sucralfate can impair levothyroxine absorption; separation and reassessment are preferable to ignoring the interaction.
Increase both drugs without changing timing
Blind dose escalation may overcorrect when timing later changes.
Crush both tablets together to improve contact
Mixing increases simultaneous contact rather than preventing binding.
Stop all thyroid monitoring because the interaction is transient
Monitoring is needed after a clinically important absorption change.
Assume sucralfate has destroyed the thyroid gland
This is an absorption interaction, not gland destruction.
